0|35c356924fe3669dfbb1185607ce3b37f70bfa80|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"mlxsw: spectrum: Fix incorrect parsing depth after reload
Spectrum ASICs have a configurable limit on how deep into the packet
they parse. By default
There are several cases where this parsing depth is not enough and there
is a need to increase it. For example
column2: timestamping of PTP packets and a

column1: FIB multipath hash policy that requires hashing on inner fields. The
driver therefore maintains a reference count that reflects the number of
consumers that require an increased parsing depth.
During reload_down() the parsing depth reference count does not
necessarily drop to zero
column2: but the parsing depth itself is restored to

column1: the default during reload_up() when the firmware is reset. It is
therefore possible to end up in situations where the driver thinks that
the parsing depth was increased (reference count is non-zero)
is not.
Fix by making sure that all the consumers that increase the parsing
depth reference count also decrease it during reload_down().
Specifically
column2: make sure that when the routing code is de-initialized it

column1: drops the reference count if it was increased because of a FIB multipath
hash policy that requires hashing on inner fields.
Add a warning if the reference count is not zero after the driver was
de-initialized and explicitly reset it to zero during initialization for
good measures.
